- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots in the next 3–5 days; apply a downward correction of 1–3%.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.1) and price is trending down, model frequently underestimates; adjust upward by 0.5–2%.
- Model tends to overreact to recent sentiment swings; smooth transitions by averaging 2–3 prior days’ forecast.
- In low-sentiment periods, model often underpredicts mean reversion; add a small upward bias (0.5–1.5%) to counteract downward drift.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often fails to capture short-term sentiment-driven reversals; use sentiment-weighted smoothing (e.g., 70% prior, 30% sentiment-adjusted).
